title: Social Security Legislation Amendment (Increased Employment Participation) Bill 2014
short_title: Social Security Legislation Amendment (Increased Employment Participation) Bill 2014

speeches.speaker: Julie Collins
speeches.brief: Discussed the Social Security Legislation Amendment (Increased Employment Participation) Bill 2014, which offers young people aged 18 to 30 a $2,500 job commitment bonus after 12 months off income support and a further $4,000 after 24 months, but criticised the bill for doubling the relocation payment's non-payment period from 12 weeks to 26 weeks for those who leave a job without good reason.

speeches.speaker: Sharman Stone
speeches.brief: Supported the bill's Job Commitment Bonus, paying $2,500 after 12 months off welfare with a further payment after another 12 months, saying youth unemployment rose from 9.9 per cent to over 12.7 per cent under Labor.

speeches.speaker: Jenny Macklin
speeches.brief: Said Labor supports the Social Security Legislation Amendment (Increased Employment Participation) Bill, citing findings that youth unemployment exceeds 12 per cent and makes up almost 40 per cent of all unemployment, and praised a Mornington Peninsula youth support program in which 70 per cent of participants moved into work or further learning.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Giles
speeches.brief: Supported the opposition's amendment to the bill, welcoming the Job Commitment Bonus and Relocation Assistance to Take Up a Job program as insufficient on their own, citing a Reserve Bank finding of a 1¼ percentage point fall in younger workers' labour force participation, and raised concerns about La Trobe University's announcement of 350 job cuts near his electorate.

speeches.speaker: Keith Pitt
speeches.brief: Supported the bill, highlighting a new Seniors Employment Incentive Payment of up to $3,250 for businesses hiring long-term unemployed people over 50, and said unemployment in his Hinkler electorate rose from six per cent under the Howard government to 9.6 per cent under Labor.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: Said Labor supports the bill's job incentives but warned they barely address youth unemployment, citing 27,300 job losses announced since the election and a government failure to guarantee funding beyond this year for the Youth Connections program, which helped 4,115 young people re-engage in education in early 2012 alone.

speeches.speaker: Brett Whiteley
speeches.brief: Supported the bill's Job Commitment Bonus, linking it to the Tasmanian employment program he launched with the employment minister, and said Tasmania's unemployment rate of 7.3 per cent and youth unemployment of 21 per cent on the state's north-west coast were the nation's worst.

speeches.speaker: Terri Butler
speeches.brief: Supported the bill as a mere fraction of what is needed, citing Brotherhood of St Laurence findings of youth unemployment hotspots in Queensland including Cairns at 20.5 per cent, and noting the Youth Connections program assisted more than 71,000 young Australians under the former Labor government.

speeches.speaker: Luke Simpkins
speeches.brief: Supported the bill's Job Commitment Bonus and Relocation Assistance to Take Up a Job program, saying youth unemployment rose from 9.9 per cent to 12.7 per cent under Labor, and noted his Cowan electorate's unemployment rate is below the Western Australian average.

speeches.speaker: Kelvin Thomson
speeches.brief: Supported the opposition's amendment, warning that unlimited 457 visas would worsen unemployment, and cited a rise in Broadmeadows unemployment from 10.3 per cent to 12.8 per cent over six months as evidence the government is failing local job seekers.

speeches.speaker: Karen McNamara
speeches.brief: Supported the bill, saying her Dobell electorate has 5,314 Newstart allowance recipients, 70 per cent of whom have received it for more than 12 months, and that around 750 could benefit from the Job Commitment Bonus and Relocation Assistance to Take Up a Job program moving off welfare.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Jones
speeches.brief: Supported the bill's up to $6,500 Job Commitment Bonus, but warned that without continued funding for programs like Better Futures in his Illawarra electorate, another generation of young people risks being left behind.

speeches.speaker: Alan Tudge
speeches.brief: Supported the bill from an Indigenous employment perspective, noting only 46 per cent of Indigenous people of working age are employed, falling to just 18 per cent among those aged 17 to 24, and said the new incentives offer up to $15,500 per family under the relocation and job commitment payments.

speeches.speaker: Sharon Claydon
speeches.brief: Supported the opposition's amendment to the bill, warning that Forgacs shipbuilder in Newcastle could lose 900 jobs without the government bringing forward naval shipbuilding contracts, and said the government had created only 33,700 of a promised 100,000 jobs after six months in office.

speeches.speaker: Sarah Henderson
speeches.brief: Supported the bill, contrasting it with what she called a failed $40 million government grant to Alcoa under the previous government, and highlighted a $5 million grant to Carbon Revolution in her Corangamite electorate that is creating 150 new jobs in carbon fibre wheel manufacturing.

speeches.speaker: Lucy Wicks
speeches.brief: Supported the Increased Employment Participation Bill, highlighting its job commitment bonus of up to $6,500 for young people who stay employed for two years and relocation assistance of up to $9,000, and cited the government's $405 million contribution to the $3 billion NorthConnex project expected to create around 2,000 jobs.

speeches.speaker: Lisa Chesters
speeches.brief: Argued Labor's support for the Increased Employment Participation Bill does not go far enough to tackle youth unemployment, citing Bendigo's 13.3 per cent unemployment rate and 400 applications for just 10 jobs at one local bacon factory, and warned proposed Fair Work Act changes could cost a cleaner earning $22.70 an hour about $100 a week in penalty rates.

speeches.speaker: David Coleman
speeches.brief: Supported the bill's job commitment bonus of up to $6,500 and relocation assistance up to $9,000, said national unemployment rose from 4.4 per cent in 2007 to 5.7 per cent in 2013 under the previous government with one in ten manufacturing jobs lost, and cited the WestConnex project's M5 East duplication as set to save at least 20 minutes travel time from his Banks electorate.

speeches.speaker: Luke Hartsuyker
speeches.brief: Summed up debate on the bill, saying youth unemployment rose from 9.9 to 12.7 per cent under the previous government leaving 55,000 more young Australians unemployed, defended the new 26-week non-payment period for those who leave a relocated job without reasonable excuse, and noted only 4 of 333 participants in the previous Move 2 Work program had ever been affected by such a penalty.

speeches.speaker: Luke Hartsuyker
speeches.brief: Moved to accept Senate amendments to the Social Security Legislation Amendment (Increased Employment Participation) Bill 2014, which provides a Job Commitment Bonus of $2,500 after 12 months in work and a further $4,000 after 24 months, plus relocation assistance of up to $6,000 for jobseekers moving to a regional area.
